facts.statement: The species Himalayasaurus tibetensis was described in 1972 based on fragmentary fossils including teeth, limb bones, and vertebrae.
facts.quote: The type species Himalayasaurus tibetensis was described in 1972 on the basis of fragmentary remains, including teeth, limb bones, and vertebrae.

facts.statement: This extinct ichthyosaur lived during the Late Triassic in the Qulonggongba Formation of Tibet.
facts.quote: Himalayasaurus is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur from the Late Triassic Qulonggongba Formation of Tibet.

facts.statement: The estimated total body length of Himalayasaurus was over 15 meters.
facts.quote: The entire body length of Himalayasaurus is estimated to have been over 15 m in length.

facts.statement: Himalayasaurus is often considered a nomen dubium due to a lack of distinguishing features, though distinct cutting edges on its teeth have been proposed as a unique trait.
facts.quote: Himalayasaurus has since been considered a nomen dubium or "dubious name" because of the lack of features that set it apart from other ichthyosaurs, although the presence of distinct cutting edges on its teeth have more recently been proposed as a unique feature of the genus

facts.statement: Himalayasaurus belongs to the family Shastasauridae, which contains other large Triassic ichthyosaurs such as Shonisaurus.
facts.quote: Himalayasaurus belongs to the family Shastasauridae, which includes other large-bodied Triassic ichthyosaurs like Shonisaurus.

facts.statement: Himalayasaurus is classified within the superorder Ichthyopterygia and the order Ichthyosauria.
Fossils of Himalayasaurus date to the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, between 215.38 and 211.18 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (215.38 to 211.18 million years ago)
